title: Muon Space raises $250 million to ramp up satellite production
summary: Muon Space has secured $250 million in funding to expand its satellite production capabilities, focusing on larger and more advanced spacecraft and constellations.

title: LatConnect 60 selects Transcelestial’s Space Optical Network for SWIRSAT imaging constellation
summary: LatConnect 60 has partnered with Transcelestial to use its Space Optical Network for the SWIRSAT-1 mission, enabling optical communications for the imaging constellation. The contract includes access to Transcelestial's optical terminal technology.

title: Draper Selects Proteus Space for Advanced On-Orbit Mission
summary: Draper Laboratory has selected Proteus Space for an advanced on-orbit mission. Proteus Space, a dual-use aerospace company, will provide rapid end-to-end access to space for the mission.

title: Hypersonic missile startup Castelion raises $1 billion
summary: Hypersonic missile startup Castelion, founded by former SpaceX executives, has raised $1 billion to develop low-cost hypersonic weapons and a broader range of strike and missile defense systems.

title: Eartheye Space forges strategic partnership with IN2
summary: Eartheye Space has signed a memorandum of understanding with IN2 to provide access to its multi-sensor satellite tasking and analytics. The strategic partnership aims to enhance IN2's capabilities in satellite data utilization.

title: Katalyst Space and NASA abandon plans for Swift reboost
summary: Katalyst Space and NASA have canceled plans to use Katalyst's Link spacecraft to boost the orbit of NASA's Swift gamma-ray observatory due to attitude-control issues with the spacecraft.

title: Moog Inc. Expands METEORITE Satellite Bus Capacity for High-Maneuverability Missions
summary: Moog Inc. has expanded the capacity of its METEORITE satellite bus to support high-maneuverability missions. This development enhances the satellite's capabilities for precision motion and control systems.

title: The space industry’s next challenge: supply chain resilience
summary: The space industry faces supply chain resilience challenges as its economy grows faster than its industrial base can support. Commercial constellations, national security architectures, and civil missions are expanding, straining existing supply chains.

title: Vantor names new head of U.S. government business
summary: Vantor has appointed Will Cocos as the new executive vice president and general manager of its U.S. government business, succeeding Susanne Hake. The move highlights Vantor's focus on expanding its Earth intelligence operations in the government sector.

title: Firefly Aerospace to fly Zeno Power radioisotope heating unit on lunar lander mission
summary: Firefly Aerospace will carry a Zeno Power radioisotope heating unit on a lunar lander mission to test technology for surviving the lunar night. The payload aims to enable future long-duration lunar missions.

title: James Webb Space Telescope finds 'hidden stars' making the universe's 1st galaxies much bigger than we knew
summary: The James Webb Space Telescope has discovered 'hidden stars' between bright stars, revealing that early galaxies are much larger than previously believed. This finding suggests that the universe's first galaxies were more massive due to the presence of these fainter stars.

title: Partial lunar eclipse live: Latest news, viewing tips and live updates from Aug. 27-28 eclipse
summary: A partial lunar eclipse occurred on August 27-28, marking the deepest one until December 2028. Live coverage included news, viewing tips, and updates.

title: A 96% partial lunar eclipse is just 1 week away: Here's what you need to know
summary: A 96% partial lunar eclipse will occur on August 27-28, with Earth's inner shadow darkening the moon's disk. This celestial event is notable for its high coverage and visibility.

title: Watch Rocket Lab launch a private Japanese Earth-observing satellite to orbit today
summary: Rocket Lab is set to launch its ninth mission for the Japanese Earth-imaging company iQPS. The launch is scheduled for Aug. 20, and the event can be watched live.

title: Scientists just found the fastest known star in the Milky Way. It zooms around our black hole at 15,500 miles per second
summary: Scientists discovered the fastest known star in the Milky Way, traveling at 15,500 miles per second around the supermassive black hole Sagittarius A*. This star is now the record-holder for the highest speed observed in our galaxy.

title: Private mission to save NASA's Swift space telescope fails
summary: A private spacecraft failed to boost NASA's Swift space telescope's orbit, leading to its planned re-entry into Earth later this year.

title: Scientists create 'laundry gun' for astronauts to clean their clothes by shooting out plasma
summary: Scientists have developed a pen-sized 'laundry gun' that uses plasma to sterilize astronauts' clothes in space. This innovation aims to address the challenge of laundry in microgravity environments.

title: 'The Mandalorian and Grogu' finally blasts onto Disney+ next month
summary: The Mandalorian and Grogu spinoff series will debut on Disney+ next month, raising questions about its potential to revitalize the franchise in the streaming space.

title: Dark matter could magnify the jets of a ravenously feeding supermassive black hole
summary: A jet from a distant supermassive black hole-powered blazar is being gravitationally lensed by an unseen clump of dark matter, potentially revealing the source of cosmic 'ghost' particles.

title: A SpaceX rocket slammed into the moon this month — and a NASA spacecraft has spotted its lunar grave (photos)
summary: A SpaceX rocket stage impacted the moon in March 2022, creating a new crater approximately 60 feet wide, which was later imaged by NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter.

title: APOD: 2026 August 20 – The Elephant’s Trunk in Cepheus
summary: The Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) for August 20, 2026, features an image titled 'The Elephant’s Trunk in Cepheus'. The post includes a brief explanation by a professional astronomer.

title: NASA TechLeap Prize: Orbital Clarity Challenge
summary: NASA's TechLeap Prize introduces the Orbital Clarity Challenge to study space weather and its impact on Earth's atmosphere. The challenge is a collaboration between NASA's Heliophysics Division, Flight Opportunities program, and Center of Excellence for Collaborative Innovation.

title: NASA Updates Next Steps for Commercial Swift Boost Mission
summary: NASA and Katalyst Space have postponed the LINK spacecraft's planned satellite boost mission due to an ongoing attitude control issue. The mission will still attempt rendezvous and proximity operations with NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory.

title: Human-Related Microbes May Survive Moon’s South Pole, NASA Finds
summary: NASA research suggests that microbes from Earth could survive in the shaded areas of the Moon's South Pole, raising concerns about potential contamination during human missions. The findings, published in Science Advances, emphasize the need for better understanding of microbial persistence in lunar environments.

title: Ancient Milky Way Merger
summary: A study using NASA's Hubble Space Telescope found definitive evidence of a dwarf galaxy merging with the young Milky Way around 12 billion years ago. The findings, published in Nature Astronomy, reveal details about this ancient galactic collision.

title: NASA Establishes State Hubs to Grow Technical Aerospace Workforce
summary: NASA has allocated $10.5 million to seven institutions to enhance state-based pathways for students into technical aerospace careers through the new NASA State Hubs initiative. This program aims to strengthen local ecosystems to accelerate workforce development in the aerospace industry.

title: Behind the Lens: Meet NASA Johnson’s Photographers
summary: NASA Johnson Space Center's photographers have documented key moments in human spaceflight, preserving history and showcasing the teams behind future missions.

title: APOD: 2026 August 19 – The Case of the Mysterious Maybe Meteor
summary: APOD (Astronomy Picture of the Day) features a daily image or photograph of the universe with an explanation by an astronomer. The image for August 19, 2026, is titled 'The Case of the Mysterious Maybe Meteor'.

title: NASA’s LRO Images Falcon 9 Crater on Moon, Learns New Details
summary: NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) captured images of a new crater on the Moon formed by a SpaceX Falcon 9 upper stage impact on Aug. 5, following the January 2025 Firefly Blue Ghost 1 mission launch.

title: Stoke Space conducts second stage fit checks, completes first stage engines ahead of Nova debut
summary: Stoke Space has completed second stage fit checks and first stage engine assembly for its Nova rocket, aiming for a debut launch in 2026. This positions the company as a competitor in the fully reusable launch vehicle market alongside SpaceX's Starship.

title: Zhuque-3 Completes Second Flight with Successful First-Stage Landing
summary: Zhuque-3, a methalox rocket developed by LandSpace, completed its second flight with a successful first-stage landing. This achievement marks a significant milestone for the company in reusable rocket technology.

title: Ship 40 arrives at Christmas Island, Plans Return to Starbase
summary: SpaceX has successfully guided Starship Ship 40 to a location just off the coast of Christmas Island. The company plans to return the ship to Starbase for further operations.

title: Launch Preview: Chang’e 7 headlines week of Chinese and Starlink launches
summary: China is preparing for the Chang'e 7 lunar mission following a recent launch failure of the Chang Zheng 7A rocket. The mission is part of a week of planned launches alongside Starlink missions.

title: Firefly promote next block of Alpha amid Eclipse progress
summary: Firefly Aerospace is advancing the development of its next-generation medium-lift rocket while also making progress on its Eclipse program. The company is promoting its next block of Alpha rockets amid these advancements.

title: Blue Origin overviews plan for dual pad ops at Cape Canaveral
summary: Blue Origin is planning dual launch pad operations at Cape Canaveral by restoring its primary launch pad at LC-36A. The company has outlined its strategy for expanded launch capabilities.

title: Rocket Lab advances via series of announcements
summary: Rocket Lab has established a new subsidiary in Germany and introduced a containerized mobile launch system. The company continues to expand its global presence and technological capabilities.

title: Amid failure, Wenchang celebrates milestone as China launches AI satellites and prepares for lunar south pole mission
summary: China's Wenchang Space Launch Site celebrated its 50th launch milestone while also experiencing a failure. The site launched AI satellites and is preparing for a lunar south pole mission.

title: Starbase Production lining up future vehicles
summary: SpaceX's Starbase production site is progressing with multiple Starship vehicles. Teams are actively working on future vehicle production.

title: Launch Preview: Chinese failure opens busy international launch salvo
summary: A Chinese launch failure marked the start of an intense week of international launches, with four launches occurring across three countries. The event highlights the competitive and high-stakes nature of the global space industry.

title: ESA Delivers: 50 years booklet
summary: ESA celebrates 50 years with a booklet highlighting 50 major achievements. The publication marks five decades of the European Space Agency's contributions to space exploration.

title: Phoenix 3: concept study for a reusable European spacecraft
summary: Engineers from ESA and industry partners completed a concept study for Phoenix 3, a reusable spacecraft for microgravity experiments and Earth return. The project aims to advance European space capabilities.

title: Proba-3’s eclipse hours before totality in Europe
summary: Proba-3 mission will create an artificial solar eclipse hours before the total solar eclipse in Europe. The mission aims to study the Sun's corona by blocking the solar disk.

title: A double eclipse for Proba-3
summary: Proba-3 will experience a double eclipse as the Moon crosses its field of view. This event is part of the mission's testing and observation phase.

title: How ESA mimics and models the 2026 total solar eclipse
summary: ESA is modeling the 2026 total solar eclipse to study the Sun's corona, using artificial eclipses and digital simulations due to the rarity and brief duration of natural eclipses.

title: Your chance to run software in deep space on ESA's asteroid mission
summary: The European Space Agency is inviting European researchers and companies to run their software aboard the Hera mission, which will travel millions of kilometers into deep space. This presents a unique opportunity for testing and validating software in a deep-space environment.

title: From drone flight to sounding rocket
summary: A student-developed radar retroreflector technology was tested for the first time using a drone at ESTEC, the European Space Agency's technical center in the Netherlands. This marks a transition from drone flight to sounding rocket applications.

title: Earth and Proba-3’s Coronagraph play hide and seek
summary: ESA's Proba-3 mission will demonstrate formation flying with two satellites to create an artificial solar eclipse for studying the Sun's corona. The coronagraph will block out the Sun's disk to reveal its outer atmosphere.

title: Meet space startups at ESA’s Industry Space Days
summary: ESA's Industry Space Days event on September 16-17 will bring together space startups and industry leaders at ESA-ESTEC in the Netherlands to exchange ideas, showcase capabilities, and explore collaborations.

title: White House Publishes S&T Strategy for National Security
summary: The White House released its National Security Science & Technology Strategy through the Office of Science and Technology Policy. This strategy aims to guide national security efforts through scientific and technological advancements.
company: White House Office of Science and Technology Policy

title: Zeno Power Books its First Nuclear Mission to the Moon
summary: Zeno Power has secured its first commercial nuclear mission to the Moon, partnering with Firefly Aerospace to launch a radioisotope heating unit on a 2028 mission. The mission, part of Firefly's CLPS CS-8 flight, aims to demonstrate Zeno's technology for maintaining power in lunar conditions.

title: Deep Dive: FY27 Defense Space Budget
summary: The Space Force's FY27 budget request has been highlighted as a record-breaking $71.3 billion. This budget request marks a significant increase in defense space spending.

title: Slingshot’s Portal Adds New AI-Powered Missions
summary: Slingshot Aerospace enhanced its Portal platform with AI-powered capabilities to improve monitoring of the increasingly crowded space environment. The update aims to assist operators in managing satellite traffic more effectively.

title: HEO Taps Planet Labs to Expand its NEI Network
summary: HEO has partnered with Planet Labs to expand its NEI network to over 50 in-space sensors, enabling more frequent and high-resolution imaging of objects in orbit from multiple angles.

title: DIU, SDA Select Winners for Deorbit-as-a-Service Designs
summary: The Space Development Agency (SDA) and Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) selected three companies to design scalable satellite capabilities for rendezvous, capture, and deorbit. This initiative aims to address space debris mitigation through a 'Deorbit-as-a-Service' approach.
company: Space Development Agency (SDA) and Defense Innovation Unit (DIU)

title: SEOPS Doubles Down on Waymaker Dedicated Rideshare Program
summary: SEOPS is expanding its Waymaker dedicated rideshare program to fill the potential gap left by SpaceX's Transporter program, which is ending. This move aims to provide cost-effective rides to orbit for space startups.

title: The New Middle Ground in Spacecraft Development
summary: The commercial space industry is shifting towards enabling customers to build their own spacecraft hardware for full mission ownership. This trend represents a new middle ground in spacecraft development beyond affordability and accessibility.

title: Exclusive: Reflect Orbital Responds to its Critics
summary: Reflect Orbital faces criticism regarding its sunlight-reflecting satellites. The company responds to the divided opinions within the space community.

title: NASA Opens Call on Moon Base Health Research
summary: NASA's Human Research Program is soliciting research proposals to address health concerns for long-term lunar stays. The initiative aims to support future Moon base missions by identifying critical health research needs.

title: TGS Taps Speedcast for All-LEO Solution
summary: Speedcast has secured a connectivity deal with TGS, implementing an all-LEO solution for their global fleet. TGS is a provider of data and intelligence services.

title: Will Cocos to Lead Vantor’s US Government Business
summary: Vantor has appointed Will Cocos as executive vice president and general manager to lead its U.S. government business. Cocos will oversee operations in U.S. defense, intelligence, and civil sectors.

title: Katalyst Link Mission is Unable to Rescue NASA Swift Observatory
summary: The Katalyst Link mission, a servicing mission to rescue NASA's Swift Observatory, has been confirmed unable to complete the rescue. NASA and Katalyst Space have acknowledged the mission's failure.

title: Kratos Reports Growing Tri-Band Antenna Demand and Debuts New Model
summary: Kratos Defense & Security Solutions has secured multi-million-dollar orders for GAIA antenna systems from international customers. The company also debuted a new model to meet growing tri-band antenna demand.

title: The Rogue Element: How Transnational Cartels Could Establish an Asymmetric Lunar Presence
summary: The Mitchell Institute for Aerospace Studies warns that the U.S. Space Force must prepare for potential lunar conflict with China, highlighting concerns over transnational cartels establishing an asymmetric lunar presence.

title: Delta Incident Puts Aviation Cybersecurity into Sharp Focus
summary: A Delta incident has highlighted the critical importance of cybersecurity in aviation in-flight connectivity (IFC) systems, which have been widely adopted by airlines to enhance passenger experience and operational efficiency.

title: Viasat Taps Rocket Lab to Build Small GEO for PTS-G Program
summary: Viasat has chosen Rocket Lab to construct a small Geostationary Orbit (GEO) satellite for its Protected Tactical Satcom-Global (PTS-G) program. The spacecraft will be based on Rocket Lab's platform.

title: Vietnam’s VinSpace Plans to Launch Tech Demonstration on 2027 SpaceX Rideshare Mission
summary: VinSpace, a space company under Vingroup, has signed a launch contract with SpaceX to deploy in-orbit demonstration satellites on a 2027 Transporter rideshare mission. This marks Vietnam's growing involvement in the global space industry through commercial partnerships.

title: Aerospace Report Examines Defense and Space Growth in FY ‘27 Budget Request
summary: A report by The Aerospace Corporation analyzes the White House's FY 2027 budget request, highlighting that over 75% of the increase is allocated to defense and space growth.

title: L3Harris Appoints Sam Mehta as New CEO After Kubasik Forced Out Due to Conduct
summary: L3Harris Technologies appointed Sam Mehta as its new president and CEO, replacing Chris Kubasik who was forced out due to conduct issues. The leadership change was effective immediately.
